paragraphs.name: Clinical details
paragraphs.normal_text: Single line after the header: age, sex, symptom, relevant risk factors or rhythm.

paragraphs.name: Technique
paragraphs.normal_text:
Non-contrast prospectively gated calcium score acquisition followed by prospectively ECG-triggered CT coronary angiography.
Heart rate 57 bpm, sinus rhythm. Metoprolol 5 mg IV. GTN 800 micrograms sublingual.
Contrast: Omnipaque 350, 60 ml.
DLP 142 mGy.cm (estimated effective dose 3.7 mSv).

paragraphs.name: Coronary arteries
paragraphs.normal_text:
Right dominant.
Normal coronary origins and course.
LMS: no plaque.
LAD: no plaque. Diagonals unremarkable.
LCx: no plaque. Obtuse marginals unremarkable.
RCA: no plaque.
No myocardial bridging.

paragraphs.name: Non-coronary findings
paragraphs.normal_text:
Cardiac chambers normal in size. No pericardial effusion.
The left atrial appendage is well opacified with no filling defect to suggest thrombus.
Ascending aorta 31 mm. Pulmonary trunk 24 mm.
Visualised lung bases unremarkable. No significant extracardiac findings.

paragraphs.name: Conclusion
paragraphs.normal_text:
1. No coronary artery calcium and no coronary plaque. CAD-RADS 0.
2. No significant non-coronary findings.

expected_per_dictation.notes: Calcium-score-only study (5 rules from one condition plus USE and the preventive APPEND). Coronary arteries section omitted entirely, taking its negatives with it. 'Cardiac chambers normal in size.' must not be emitted (LA dilated). Effective dose 41 x 0.026 = 1.1 mSv. Conclusion should mirror 05: very high calcium burden, CTCA not performed and why, preventive therapy, further assessment guided by symptoms. No CAD-RADS category should be invented.
Entirely normal: report should match 01 almost line for line (Total Agatston score 0., CAD-RADS 0, two-item conclusion). Effective dose 121 x 0.026 = 3.1 mSv. No IF_PRESENT negative (no plaque).

negatives_omitted: The left atrial appendage is well opacified with no filling defect to suggest thrombus.
expected_per_dictation.notes: Tricky: the anomaly is described without the word 'anomalous' (RCA from the left coronary sinus, interarterial course, slit-like proximal segment), so the plain NEGATIVE 'Normal coronary origins and course.' must flip to OMIT and be replaced by a described anomalous origin - and the conclusion must report it despite CAD-RADS 0 and zero calcium; 'No significant non-coronary findings.' may stand but the conclusion must not read as a normal study. The LAA tip is dictated colloquially ('doesn't fill on this phase') in sinus rhythm - REPLACE and its conclusion APPEND still apply. No plaque, so P32 (preventive therapy) is NOT met and no 'No high-risk plaque features.' is written. Effective dose 158 x 0.026 = 4.1 mSv.
